diagnosis.what_happened: In correlation matrix tables, the variable number, name, and subscale were compressed into a single initial column (e.g. '۱. رفتارهای خودآسیبی کلی'), obscuring construct hierarchy and cluttering table cells.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Combining row index, parent construct, and subscale dimension into one flat column reduced structural transparency and diverged from institutional Persian thesis formatting.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: All correlation matrix tables must feature exactly 3 descriptive lead columns before the numbered correlation columns: Column 1 ('ردیف' / num), Column 2 ('متغیر' / variable), and Column 3 ('خرده‌مقیاس' / subscale).
diagnosis.rationale_why: A 3-column pre-numbering structure clearly separates index numbering, primary construct, and subscale components, adhering to the highest standards of APA 7 Persian psychometric reporting.

desired_behavior: Structure all correlation matrices with: Col 1 ('ردیف'), Col 2 ('متغیر'), Col 3 ('خرده‌مقیاس'), followed by correlation columns ('۱', '۲', '۳', ...).
generalization: Every bivariate or psychometric correlation matrix in AcademicSuite must lead with the 3-column layout: [ردیف, متغیر, خرده‌مقیاس].

evidence.observed_value: In the correlation tables, you should have 3 columns beform numbering columns. 1. num, 2. variable, 3. subscale.
